positive_class_why: Minority class (24%) and the class of interest; PR metrics are computed for it.

missing_label.why: 3 train / 1 test rows have no label; a label cannot be imputed without inventing ground truth, and 4 rows are <0.01% of the data.

missing_indicators.why: Feature missingness is tiny (<=7 cells per column) so median/own-level imputation is safe; the indicator is kept mainly because zero-as-missing (below) routes the structural-zero blocks into it.

categorical_missing.why: Missing categorical cells get their own '__missing__' level instead of the mode, so the model - not the imputer - decides whether missingness matters; with <=7 rows per column this cannot distort the distribution.

zero_as_missing.why: Zeros come in blocks: performance_score and stability_index are 0 together in 265 rows (all 'no'); load_ratio and activity_duration are 0 together in 38 rows. Exact co-occurring zeros in otherwise continuous measures mark a structurally different group (e.g. 'no activity recorded') rather than the low end of a continuum. Converting them to NaN + missing indicator isolates that group in one binary feature (which keeps the all-'no' signal) and removes the point mass at 0 that would bend a linear fit. Tested for both models (A1, A2).

rare_level_threshold.why: 17 of 21 region levels (4.8% of rows together) and a few era/mineral levels are below 1%; pooling them into one 'infrequent' level avoids one-hot columns estimated from <300 rows and handles unseen test levels gracefully.

placeholder_levels.why: 'Other'/'Unknown' in region, personal_interest and species have distinct positive rates (e.g. species=Unknown 8.7% vs 24% overall), so they carry information and are kept as ordinary levels rather than recoded to missing.

log_transform.why: No numeric column has |skew| >= 2; clipping (LR only) is enough for the tails.

drop_columns.why: Global: nothing dropped; the composite_rank decision is model-specific (see models).

cv.why: Stratified 5-fold keeps the 24% prevalence in every fold (~6.2k validation rows each, enough for stable AP). Average precision (PR-AUC) is threshold-free and focuses on the minority class, whereas accuracy would reward the 76% majority baseline.

threshold.why: Class costs are unknown, so the operating threshold is chosen to maximise F1 of the positive class on out-of-fold training predictions - never on the test set. Metrics at 0.5 are reported as well.

models.label: Logistic Regression

drop_columns.why: composite_rank = 0.006*aptitude + 0.004*performance exactly (R^2=0.9999999). For a linear model it adds no information and makes the coefficient vector non-identifiable; dropping it loses nothing because LR can rebuild it.

clip_quantiles.why: load_ratio, index_weight and activity_duration have 1.8%, 0.5% and 3.8% of values beyond 3*IQR (maxima 143.7, 99.6, 205 vs medians 23.7, 11.7, 80.3); a linear logit is unbounded in x, so a few extreme points can dominate. Quantiles are learned inside each training fold.

models.why: Transparent linear baseline: tells us how much of the signal is additive in the (one-hot) features. Probabilities are calibrated only if class_weight=None wins the search. Stopping: lbfgs until gradient tolerance 1e-4 (max 5000 iterations, convergence checked).

models.label: Hist. Gradient Boosting

clip_quantiles.why: Trees split on order statistics, so monotone clipping cannot change them.

models.why: Captures non-linearities and interactions (e.g. weather x instrument) that LR cannot; native categorical splits avoid a 80-column one-hot; keeps composite_rank because axis-aligned trees cannot synthesise a linear combination themselves. Stopping: early stopping on a 10% internal validation split when log-loss fails to improve for 30 rounds. min_samples_leaf searched up to 600 (~n/50) because with 25k rows per training fold a leaf of a few hundred rows is still a small fraction of the data and acts as the main regulariser.

ablations.question: LR: keep co-occurring zeros as values (no NaN + indicator)
HGB: keep co-occurring zeros as values (no NaN + indicator)
LR: no winsorising of heavy tails
HGB: one-hot instead of native categorical splits

high_correlation.why: performance_score/stability_index r=0.89 and both with composite_rank r>=0.83 are below the exact-dependency level; dropping would discard information and L2 regularisation (LR) / greedy splits (HGB) cope with it. Caveat for interpretation: LR coefficients and permutation importances are shared among these correlated columns.
